Dehumanization
dee-hyoo-muh-nuh-ZAY-shuhn
noun
The treating of human beings as less than human; from the Latin de-, removal, and humanus, human.

📖 Biblical Definition

Dehumanization is the sin of regarding and treating a human being as less than human—denying in word, thought, or deed the dignity that belongs to every person as a bearer of the image of God. Scripture grounds the worth of man not in his usefulness, his strength, his stage of development, or his group, but in creation: God made man in His own image, and crowned him with glory and honor, a little lower than the angels. This is why the shedding of innocent blood is so grave—whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed, for in the image of God made He man—and why the tongue that curses men made after the similitude of God is condemned. To oppress the poor is to reproach his Maker. Every great cruelty of history has begun by first denying the full humanity of its victims: the slave reduced to property, the unborn child reckoned a clump of cells, the aged and disabled judged a burden not worth living, the enemy painted as vermin to be exterminated. The dictionary names dehumanization as a root sin against the imago Dei, and holds up against it the unwavering biblical truth that every human being—born and unborn, strong and weak, friend and foe—bears the image of God and is owed the honor, protection, and love due an image-bearer of the Almighty.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The sin of treating a human being as less than human; answered by the truth that every person bears the image of God and is crowned with glory and honor.

Gen 9:6 — "Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man."

Jas 3:9 — "Therewith bless we God, even the Father; and therewith curse we men, which are made after the similitude of God."

Pro 14:31 — "He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker: but he that honoureth him hath mercy on the poor."

Psa 8:5 — "For thou hast made him a little lower than the angels, and hast crowned him with glory and honour."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition, though “dignity” is severed from its ground in the imago Dei; the worth of man rests on creation, and dehumanization is sin against the image of God.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The matter to weigh is the ground of human worth. The secular age affirms “human dignity” loudly but cannot account for it, having cut it loose from its only sure foundation—that man is made in the image of God. A dignity grounded merely in usefulness, autonomy, or social consensus is a dignity that can be revoked when a life is judged inconvenient; and so the same age that proclaims human rights dehumanizes the unborn child, the dying, and the disabled when they cost too much. Without the imago Dei, “dignity” is a sentiment with no defense against the strong who would deny it to the weak.

The principle to recover is the image of God as the unshakable ground of every human life’s worth. Man is crowned with glory and honor by his Maker; his blood may not be shed because he is made in God’s image; the tongue may not curse him because he is made in God’s likeness; the poor may not be oppressed because to do so reproaches his Maker. Dehumanization—whether of the slave, the unborn, the enemy, or the outcast—is sin against the Almighty whose image the victim bears. The church honors God by honoring every image-bearer, born and unborn, strong and weak, friend and foe.
